emails.subject: Welcome aboard, Nathan Carr
emails.body:
Settle in.

The task-api incident sits on the table. Sam's first briefing on the left explains the rollback and where your runtime sits now — start there once you've run the commands in the email below.

Your start time just got logged for event SLC-001 (issue #101). Credit allocation goes to the facilitator's queue; once credits post, the agent is live on your fork.

Read the briefings in order, then fork and ship a PR. We'll keep score.

emails.subject: Run these four commands to set up your runtime
emails.body:
Here's the actual getting-started sheet. Five steps, ~3 minutes.

## 1. Get the repo

```
git clone https://github.com/castai/kimchi-workshop.git
cd kimchi-workshop
```

## 2. Make a clean environment

```
python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

## 3. Run the tests

```
python -m pytest tests/ -q
```

Expected output: `4 failed, 5 passed`. That red is your starting position — the four failed tests are where the hasty hot-patch broke the spec.

## 4. Read the incident before you change anything

Open `PRODUCTION-INCIDENT.md` in the repo root. It explains what the service is supposed to do and why the previous patcher failed.

## 5. Set your identity

Run `kimchi` in the repo root and say yes when it asks to trust the project. Then `/tags add attendee:<your-github-handle>` — that's how your spend gets attributed when the leaderboard scores you.

Once the four red are green, you're ready for the briefings on the left rail. Start with Sam's incident brief.

— Marcus
